intro: You are at Anıtkabir, in Ankara province, built in 1944–1953: the mausoleum of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. As you follow the Lion Road climbing to the ceremonial court, notice how Hittite and Seljuk forms are drawn into a deliberately plain language of stone.
history: After Atatürk's death in 1938, an international competition was opened, and Emin Onat and Orhan Arda won it. Built between 1944 and 1953 on Rasattepe above Ankara, the monument reduces forms drawn from Hittite lions to Seljuk stonework into a deliberately plain monumental language. On 10 November 1953, Atatürk was moved here.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Lion Road and the Ceremonial Plaza, then the Hall of Honour, the Atatürk and War of Independence Museum, and the ten towers.
facts: Did you know? The stone of the ceremonial plaza was brought from every part of the country, and the twenty-four lions of the Lion Road are carved seated, in the Hittite manner. The monument stands on Rasattepe above Ankara, and the building work uncovered Phrygian tumuli beneath the hill.
outro: This brings our tour of Anıtkabir to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for visiting with respect, and farewell.
